questions.prompt: The ancient manuscript was so fragile that the historian handled it with ___ care.
questions.explanation:
(a) utmost
‘Utmost’ means extreme. The given
sentence states that due to the fragility
of the manuscript, the historian handled
it with extreme care. Hence, ‘utmost’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The abstruse philosophical treatise delved ______ the very essence of existentialism.
questions.explanation:
(a) into
‘Into’ is a fixed preposition used with the
verb ‘delve’. Hence, ‘into’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Despite initial optimism, the second attempt at the experiment was ______ successful than the first.
questions.explanation:
(b) less
'Less' is the comparative form of 'little'
and is used here to compare the success
of the second attempt with the first. The
sentence indicates a reduced level of
success in the second attempt. Hence,
'less' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You can either submit your research paper today _____ by the end of the week.
questions.explanation:
(c) or
‘Either…or’ is a fixed conjunction pair.
Hence, ‘or’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The venerable professor, ______ lectures always captivated his students, announced his retirement.
questions.explanation:
(c) whose
'Whose' is a relative adjective used to
refer to people or things, indicating
possession. In this sentence, the lectures
belong to the professor, so 'whose'
correctly shows this relationship. Hence,
‘whose’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The incessant debate began to ______ the enthusiasm of even the most dedicated participants.
questions.explanation:
(c) enervate
'Enervate' means to cause (someone) to
feel drained of energy or vitality. The
given sentence states that the incessant
debate began to enervate the
enthusiasm of even the most dedicated
participants. Hence, ‘enervate’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: So intricate______the machinery that even experts took hours to assemble it.
questions.explanation:
(b) was
This sentence is an example of inversion
for emphasis, where the auxiliary verb
precedes the subject. The subject
“machinery” is singular, so the verb must
also be singular. Hence, “was” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: His explanation was ____ than confusing; it was a tangled mess of ideas.
questions.explanation:
(b) more
The word "more" is used here to
emphasize that his explanation went
beyond merely being confusing,
suggesting it was an even greater degree
of disorganization and lack of clarity.
Hence, "more" is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The leader's speech, meant to inspire unity, instead managed to _______ further division among the already fractured factions.
questions.explanation:
(b) foment
The word "foment" means to instigate or
stir up (an undesirable or violent
sentiment or course of action), which
perfectly fits the context of stirring up
division. Hence, "foment" is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Hardly ever______the opportunity to witness such a rare celestial event.
questions.explanation:
(b) do we have
When a sentence begins with a negative
adverbial phrase (like 'hardly ever',
'scarcely', 'never', 'seldom', 'rarely'),
inversion of the subject and auxiliary
verb is required for emphasis. Therefore,
'do we have' is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The detective's unwavering commitment to justice often led him to pursue cases with unbridled ______.
questions.explanation:
(c) zealotry
‘Zealotry’ means extreme devotion. The
given sentence states that the detective’s
unwavering commitment to justice often
led him to pursue cases with unbridled
zealotry. Hence, ‘zealotry’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The constant dripping of water began to ____the stone, eroding it slowly over centuries.
questions.explanation:
(c) abrade
'Abrade' means to scrape or wear away
by friction or erosion. The given sentence
states that the constant dripping of
water began to abrade the stone, eroding
it slowly over centuries. Hence, ‘abrade’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Although the expedition was fraught with peril, they encountered ______ challenges than anticipated.
questions.explanation:
(a) fewer
‘Fewer’ is a comparative degree used
with plural countable nouns. Similarly, in
the given sentence, ‘challenges’ is a
plural countable noun. Hence, ‘fewer’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The new software promised to streamline operations; ______, initial implementation proved unexpectedly complex.
questions.explanation:
(c) however
'However' is an adverb used to introduce
a statement that contrasts with or
contradicts something that has been
said previously. Here, it presents a
contrast between the promise of
streamlined operations and complex
implementation. Hence, ‘however’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If not for the early warning system, the city would have ______significant damage from the tsunami.
questions.explanation:
(a) sustained
'Sustained' means to suffer (something
unpleasant, especially an injury, a defeat,
or a loss). The given sentence states that
the city would have sustained significant
damage from the tsunami if not for the
early warning system. Hence, ‘sustained’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The constant criticism from his peers ______ him to rethink his approach.
questions.explanation:
(d) motivates
In the given sentence, ‘the constant
criticism’ is a singular subject that will
take ‘motivates’ as a singular verb.
Hence, ‘motivates’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The diplomat was adept _________ negotiating complex international treaties.
questions.explanation:
(a) at
‘At’ is a fixed preposition used with
‘adept’. Hence, 'at' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct. By the time the rescue team ______ at the site, most of the villagers had already been evacuated to safer ground.
questions.explanation:
(d) arrived
If two actions took place in the past then
the 1st action must be in the Past perfect
tense(Had + V 3) and the 2nd action must
be in the Simple Past tense(V 2). In the
given sentence, ‘evacuation’ is the 1st
action & ‘arrival’ is the 2nd action. Hence,
‘arrived(V 2)’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The committee reviewed all the proposals, none of _____ met the required criteria.
questions.explanation:
(b) which
"Which" is a relative pronoun used to
introduce a non-restrictive clause that
refers to things or animals. In this case,
"which" refers back to "proposals." Hence,
“which” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Hardly _______the team completed the report when the boss called them for a presentation.
questions.explanation:
(c) had
If a sentence starts with a negative word
(hardly / barely / scarcely / rarely / no
sooner / not only / never / little), the
correct grammatical structure is
“Negative word + Helping verb + Subject
+ Main Verb”. The sentence describes an
action completed before another past
action, so it requires Past Perfect Tense
(had + V3). Hence, “had” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The scientist’s conclusions were entirely _____ to the data presented in the report.
questions.explanation:
(a) Contradictory
The word “contradictory” means
opposite or inconsistent with something
else. The sentence suggests that the
scientist’s conclusions did not agree with
the data in the report. Hence,
“Contradictory” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner had the curtain fallen _____the audience erupted into applause.
questions.explanation:
(c) than
“No sooner–than” is the fixed
conjunction pair. Hence, ‘than’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: ______ having been warned about the risks, she proceeded with the experimental procedure.
questions.explanation:
(a) In spite of
"In spite of" is a prepositional phrase
meaning "despite" or "regardless of." It
correctly conveys a contrast between
being warned and proceeding with the
action. Hence, "In spite of" is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The committee recommended that the new policy _________ implemented immediately.
questions.explanation:
(c) be
The given sentence uses the subjunctive
mood after verbs like recommendation,
demand, suggest, etc. The subjunctive
mood requires the base form of the verb.
Hence, "be" is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The new manager promised to _____ the old, inefficient procedures with more modern methods.
questions.explanation:
(d) do away with
The phrasal verb ‘do away with’ means to
get rid of something. The given sentence
states that the new manager promised to
get rid of the old, inefficient procedures
and replace them with more modern
methods. Hence, ‘do away with’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The party leader appealed to the electorate to consider the long-term implications _____ the proposed reforms.
questions.explanation:
(b) of
‘Of’ means relating to something. The
given sentence talks about implications
related to the proposed reforms. Hence,
‘of’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The new policy proved to be entirely ______to the needs of the working class, exacerbating existing inequalities.
questions.explanation:
(c) detrimental
‘Entirely’ is an adverb which modifies an
adjective coming after it. ‘Detrimental is
an adjective which takes the preposition
‘to’ after it. Hence, ‘detrimental’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Not until the results were officially announced ____ the students celebrate.
questions.explanation:
(b) did they
The given sentence is an example of
inversion, which often occurs with "not
until" at the beginning of a sentence. The
auxiliary verb (did) comes before the
subject (they). Hence, “did they” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The scientist, ____ discovery changed the course of modern medicine, was awarded the Nobel Prize.
questions.explanation:
(c) whose
"Whose" is a possessive pronoun that
refers to the scientist's discovery. Hence,
“whose” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The committee reached a _____ decision after hours of intense discussion.
questions.explanation:
(c) well-thought-out
The collocation “well-thought-out” means
carefully considered or planned in detail
before being implemented. Hence, option
c is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The proposal, ________ was initially dismissed, later gained widespread approval.
questions.explanation:
(b) which
The relative pronoun “which” is used to
add non-defining information about the
proposal. Hence, “which” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Had he arrived on time, he _____the beginning of the presentation.
questions.explanation:
(b) would have caught
The given sentence is an example of the
third conditional sentence and “had + V 3
... would have + V 3 ” is the correct
grammatical structure for it. Hence,
‘would have caught (V 3 )’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Despite ample resources being allocated, bureaucratic inefficiencies continued to ______the project's progress.
questions.explanation:
(d) impede
‘Impede’ means to interfere with the
activity or progress of something. The
given sentence states that bureaucratic
inefficiencies continued to impede the
project’s progress despite ample
resources being allocated. Hence,
‘impede’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The health of an ecosystem is directly proportional _____the diversity of species it supports.
questions.explanation:
(c) to
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the
word ‘proportional’. Hence, ‘to’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrasal verb: After hours of discussion, they finally __________ a reasonable solution.
questions.explanation:
(a) came up with
The phrasal verb “came up with” means
to think of or produce an idea, plan, or
solution. In the given sentence, the
context suggests that after a long
discussion, the people involved were able
to think of or suggest a reasonable
solution. Hence, “came up with” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The scientist’s theory was praised for its originality but criticized for the ______ of supporting evidence.
questions.explanation:
(a) paucity
The word “paucity,” means a small
amount or scarcity of something. The
given sentence states that the scientist’s
theory was praised for its originality but
criticized for the lack of supporting
evidence. Hence, “paucity” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She had to _____ her previous statements after new evidence emerged.
questions.explanation:
(a) take back
‘Take back’ means to withdraw
something said. The given sentence
states that she had to take back her
previous statements after new evidence
emerged. Hence, ‘take back’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the correct part of speech to fill in the blank: Despite the unexpected challenges, the team remained ______focused on their objective.
questions.explanation:
(b) resolutely
The given sentence requires an adverb to
modify the adjective 'focused'.
‘Resolutely’ is an adverb, meaning in a
determined way. Hence, ‘resolutely’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Seldom ______ so many people interested in a poetry reading.
questions.explanation:
(a) have I seen
The adverb “seldom” is a negative word
that causes inversion i.e., the auxiliary
verb comes before the subject. Hence,
“have I seen” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Not until the evidence was re-examined did the scientist fully____the implications of her discovery.
questions.explanation:
(a) apprehend
The word “Apprehend” means to
understand or grasp the meaning of
something. The given sentence states
that the scientist did not fully understand
or grasp the implications of her discovery
until the evidence was re-examined.
Hence, “Apprehend” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Although the proposal appeared promising at first, further analysis revealed it to be _____ in logic.
questions.explanation:
(b) Fallacious
The word "Fallacious" means based on a
mistaken belief, illogical, or unsound. The
given sentence implies that initial
impressions were positive, but further
analysis uncovered flaws. Hence,
“Fallacious” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The philosopher's discourse was so _____ that only a handful of scholars could fully comprehend its nuanced intricacies.
questions.explanation:
(c) recondite
‘Recondite’ means difficult to understand
for one having ordinary knowledge. The
given sentence states that the
philosopher’s discourse was so recondite
that only a handful of scholars could fully
comprehend its nuanced intricacies.
Hence, ‘recondite’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The detective had to ______ many clues to solve the complex case.
questions.explanation:
(c) piece together
‘Piece together’ means to understand
something by combining individual
pieces of information. The given
sentence states that the detective had to
piece together many clues to solve the
complex case. Hence, ‘piece together’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Hardly had the train left the station ______ it started raining heavily.
questions.explanation:
(a) when
“Hardly….when” is a fixed conjunction
pair. Hence, “when” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The historian often alluded ______ ancient myths in his lectures, enriching the narrative .
questions.explanation:
(c) to
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the
verb ‘allude’. Hence, ‘to’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The old factory will be ______ into a modern art gallery next year.
questions.explanation:
(b) turned into
‘Turned into’ means transformed into
something else. The given sentence
states that the old factory will be turned
into a modern art gallery next year.
Hence, ‘turned into’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: If they ______ the warning, they wouldn't have made that mistake.
questions.explanation:
(b) had heeded
The given sentence is an example of a
third conditional sentence and the
correct grammatical structure for it is “If
+ past perfect (had + V 3 )…….. Would have
+ V 3 ”. Hence, “had heeded” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The artist's ______ brushstrokes captured the essence of the landscape.
questions.explanation:
(a) masterful
The given sentence requires an adjective
to describe the 'brushstrokes'. 'Masterful'
is an adjective, which means performed
with the skill of a master. Hence,
‘masterful’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The professor, ______ reputation for rigorous research was widely known, retired last year.
questions.explanation:
(c) whose
'Whose' is a relative adjective denoting a
sense of possession or belonging. The
given sentence states that the professor,
whose reputation for rigorous research
was widely known, retired last year.
Hence, ‘whose’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct semantic fit: The committee’s decision was a major ______ in the company’s expansion plans.
questions.explanation:
(b) Setback
The word “Setback” means an obstacle
or delay in progress. The given sentence
implies that the committee’s decision
had a negative impact on the company’s
expansion plans. Hence, “Setback” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the correct form of the verb. The prevalence of infectious diseases among vulnerable populations ______ a constant concern for public health organisations.
questions.explanation:
(d) remains
The true subject of the sentence is
'prevalence' (singular), not 'populations'
(plural). The phrase "of infectious
diseases among vulnerable populations"
is a prepositional phrase. Therefore, the
verb must agree with the singular subject
'prevalence'. 'Remains' is the correct
singular verb for simple present tense.
Hence, ‘remains’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The ancient scroll, previously thought to be lost, ______ in a hidden chamber.
questions.explanation:
(a) was discovered
The given sentence describes a past
event where the scroll was found. Since,
‘the scroll’ is the object of the action (it
didn't discover itself), the passive voice is
required. ‘Was + V 3 ’ is the correct passive
structure for simple past tense. Hence,
‘was discovered(V 3 )’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The manager handled the crisis so _____that everyone praised his calmness.
questions.explanation:
(a) Efficiently
"Efficiently" is the adverb form of
"efficient" and means "in a well-organized
and productive manner." The given
sentence describes how the manager
handled the crisis, which requires an
adverb to modify the verb "handled."
Hence, "efficiently" is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Her calm demeanor in the face of chaos acted like ______ for the anxious team members.
questions.explanation:
(c) reassurance
‘Reassurance’ means the act of relieving
someone of anxiety. The given sentence
states that her calm demeanor in the
face of chaos acted as a reassurance for
the team members. Hence, ‘reassurance’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After a long journey, they decided to ______ for the night at a small inn.
questions.explanation:
(b) put up
‘Put up’ means to stay somewhere for a
short time. The given sentence states
that after a long journey, they decided to
put up for the night at a small in. Hence,
‘put up’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The journalist was praised for her _______ investigation into the corruption scandal.
questions.explanation:
(a) meticulous
“Meticulous” means showing great
attention to detail; very careful and
precise. In the given sentence, the word
qualifies the noun investigation,
indicating that the journalist’s work was
careful, thorough, and detailed. Hence,
“meticulous” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Scarcely had the CEO signed the contract ____ the company announced the merger.
questions.explanation:
(a) when
“Scarcely-when” is the fixed conjunction
pair. Hence, “CEO signed the contract
when the company” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He was remembered not for what he said but ____he refrained from saying.
questions.explanation:
(d) for what
The given sentence is a contrastive
statement that emphasizes the
difference between what he spoke and
what he deliberately refrained from
saying. Hence, “for what” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: ________ his rigorous training, the athlete struggled to complete the marathon.
questions.explanation:
(d) Despite
‘Despite’ is used to introduce a
contrasting statement that does not
affect the main event. Similarly, in the
given sentence, his rigorous training did
not help him complete the marathon.
Hence, ‘Despite’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: This movie is not ______ interesting as the book it was based on.
questions.explanation:
(c) so
The given sentence is a negative
comparison, and the correct structure is
“not so…as”, which is used to compare
two things when the first is less than the
second. Hence, “so” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Not until the auditors had submitted their exhaustive report ______ the full extent of procedural lapses become evident.
questions.explanation:
(a) did
This is an example of inversion, which
occurs when a sentence begins with a
negative or restrictive expression such
as "only after," "never," or "hardly." In these
cases, the auxiliary verb comes before
the subject. Hence, “did” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The manager felt caught _____ a rock and a hard place when he had to choose between laying off staff or cutting salaries.
questions.explanation:
(b) between
‘Caught between a rock and a hard place’
is the correct idiom. Hence, ‘between’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The novel was ______ complex for young readers to understand fully.
questions.explanation:
(b) too
The adverb “too” is used to indicate that
something has an excessive degree of a
particular quality, resulting in a negative
consequence. The structure “too +
adjective + to + verb” is appropriate here
because it shows that the novel’s
complexity exceeds a level that prevents
young readers from fully understanding
it. Hence, “too” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The generous severance package was commensurate______his long and dedicated service to the company.
questions.explanation:
(b) with
‘With’ is a fixed preposition used after the
adjective ‘commensurate’ to indicate
proportion or correspondence. Hence,
‘commensurate with’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Hardly had the game started ______ the rain began to pour.
questions.explanation:
(a) when
‘Hardly…when’ is a fixed conjunction pair.
Hence, ‘when’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: ______ the sun set, the temperature began to drop.
questions.explanation:
(a) When
When indicates that one event happened
at the time another began. In the given
sentence, the event of the temperature
beginning to drop happened after the sun
set. Hence, “when” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The minister addressed the issue _________, ensuring no misunderstanding remained.
questions.explanation:
(b) unambiguously
The adverb “unambiguously” means
clearly or without any doubt. In the given
sentence, the minister addressed the
issue in a clear and definite manner so
that no misunderstanding remained.
Hence, “unambiguously” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: No sooner had the referee blown the whistle ______the match officials intervened.
questions.explanation:
(b) than
‘No sooner … than’ is a fixed conjunction
pair. Hence, ‘than’ is the most appropriate
Answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the correct noun form of the word to fill in the blank. The detective's brilliant _____ led him to the solution of the complex crime.
questions.explanation:
(a) ratiocination
‘Ratiocination’ is the correct spelling,
meaning the process of exact thinking;
reasoning. (Correct)

questions.prompt: While the students _____on their research projects, the professor entered the lab.
questions.explanation:
(b) were working
The given sentence describes an action
that occurred while another action was in
progress. The action that was in
progress in the past is written in past
continuous tense. ‘Students’ is a plural
subject, therefore the plural helping verb
‘were’ will be used. Hence, ‘were working’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate article. In ______ event of a system failure, employees must follow ________ protocol established by the IT department.
questions.explanation:
(c) an, the
“An” is used before “event” because it is a
singular, countable noun that starts with
a vowel sound and refers to any possible
occurrence of a system failure. “The” is
used before “protocol” because it refers
to a specific set of rules already
established by the IT department. Hence,
“an, the” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill the correct degree of comparison: Of all the remedies suggested, this treatment seems the _______.
questions.explanation:
(b) most effective
When comparing one thing with all
others, we use the superlative degree of
comparison. The sentence uses "of all
the remedies suggested" which indicates
a comparison among more than two
things. "Most effective" is the superlative
form of "effective." Hence, “most
effective” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The team performed ______ well that they broke all previous records.
questions.explanation:
(b) so
"So... that" is a common correlative
conjunction structure used to show
cause and effect. Hence, “so” is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She wants to buy _____ new dress for ______ party next week.
questions.explanation:
(a) a, the
For the first blank, 'new dress' is a
singular countable noun and is being
introduced for the first time, so 'a' is
appropriate. For the second blank, 'party
next week' refers to a specific party
known to the speaker, therefore the
article ‘the’ will be used before it. Hence,
‘a, the’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: She wants to become ______ engineer and work on renewable energy projects.
questions.explanation:
(b) an
Article ‘an’ is used before words starting
with a vowel sound(an apple, an
engineer, an umbrella). Hence, ‘an’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The teacher advised revising the entire syllabus ______ than focusing on a single topic.
questions.explanation:
(b) rather
The phrase “rather than” is used to
indicate a preference or contrast
between two actions or ideas. In the
given sentence, it shows a preference for
revising everything instead of
concentrating on a single topic. Hence,
“rather” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The archaeologist unearthed _______ancient artefact, providing _______ invaluable glimpse into ______ prehistoric civilization.
questions.explanation:
(b) an, an, a
For the first blank, 'ancient' starts with a
vowel sound, so 'an' is appropriate. For
the second blank, 'invaluable' starts with
a vowel sound, so 'an' is also appropriate.
For the third blank, 'prehistoric
civilization' is being introduced as one
example, not a specific or previously
mentioned one, so 'a' is correct. Hence,
‘an, an, a’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the appropriate collocation: The CEO ______ a speech at the annual conference.
questions.explanation:
(d) delivered
‘Deliver a speech’ is the correct
collocation. Hence, ‘delivered’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The ancient city, ______ ruins lay buried beneath centuries of sand, was once a thriving metropolis.
questions.explanation:
(b) whose
The blank requires a possessive relative
pronoun to link 'ruins' to 'the ancient city',
indicating that the ruins belong to the
city. 'Whose' is the correct relative
pronoun to express possession. Hence,
‘whose’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct tense: By next week, they ________ launched the new product.
questions.explanation:
(a) will have
In this sentence, the future perfect tense
is used to indicate that an action will be
completed before a specific point in the
future. The structure of the future perfect
tense is ‘will have’ + the past participle of
the main verb. Here, the verb ‘launch’ in
its past participle form is ‘launched.’
Hence, ‘will have’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After weeks of resistance, the smaller company had to ______to the demands of the larger corporation.
questions.explanation:
(d) knuckle under
‘Knuckle under’ means to submit or yield
to the demands of someone. The given
sentence states that after weeks of
resistance, the smaller company had to
knuckle under to the demands of the
larger corporation. Hence, ‘knuckle under’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Scarcely had the alarm sounded ______ the building was evacuated.
questions.explanation:
(b) when
‘Scarcely…when’ is a fixed conjunction
pair. Hence, ‘when’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: She tried to ____the sensitive information during the meeting.
questions.explanation:
(a) play down
The phrasal verb “play down” means to
make something seem less important or
significant. In the given sentence, she
attempted to minimize the importance of
the sensitive information. Hence, “play
down” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence by using the correct collocation. Due to his family connections on the board, John seemed to _______ in the promotion race, leaving other qualified candidates at a disadvantage.
options: lay his cards on the table
questions.explanation:
(a) hold all the cards
‘Hold all the cards’ is an idiom which
means to be in a strong, advantageous
position, often implying that one has an
unfair advantage or control due to
circumstances (like family connections).
Hence, ‘hold all the cards’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrasal verb: After hours of discussion, the committee ______ a decision regarding the budget allocation.
questions.explanation:
(b) arrived at
The phrasal verb “arrive at” is used when
referring to reaching a conclusion,
decision, or agreement. In the given
sentence, the committee reached a
decision regarding the budget allocation.
Hence, “arrived at” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Although the proposal appeared promising at first, further analysis revealed it to be _______ in logic.
questions.explanation:
(b) Fallacious
The word "Fallacious" means based on a
mistaken belief, illogical, or unsound. The
given sentence implies that initial
impressions were positive, but further
analysis uncovered flaws. Hence,
“Fallacious” is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Not until the auditors had submitted their exhaustive report ______ the full extent of procedural lapses become evident.
questions.explanation:
(a) did
This is an example of inversion, which
occurs when a sentence begins with a
negative or restrictive expression such
as "only after," "never," or "hardly." In these
cases, the auxiliary verb comes before
the subject. Hence, “did” is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The government's new policies sought to ______ economic growth, not stifle it.
questions.explanation:
(c) stimulate
‘Stimulate’ means to encourage
something to grow. The given sentence
states that the government’s new
policies sought to stimulate economic
growth, not stifle it. Hence, ‘stimulate’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The new manager promised to _____ the old, inefficient procedures with more modern methods.
questions.explanation:
(d) do away with
The phrasal verb ‘do away with’ means to
get rid of something. The given sentence
states that the new manager promised to
get rid of the old, inefficient procedures
and replace them with more modern
methods. Hence, ‘do away with’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The ancient scroll, previously thought to be lost, ______ in a hidden chamber.
questions.explanation:
(a) was discovered
The given sentence describes a past
event where the scroll was found. Since,
‘the scroll’ is the object of the action (it
didn't discover itself), the passive voice is
required. ‘Was + V 3’ is the correct passive
structure for simple past tense. Hence,
‘was discovered(V )’ is the most
3
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Hardly had the game started ______ the rain began to pour.
questions.explanation:
(a) when
‘Hardly…when’ is a fixed conjunction pair.
Hence, ‘when’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate phrasal verb: The argument became heated, and the mediator attempted to _______ it ________.
questions.explanation:
(c) cool down
The phrasal verb “cool down” means to
reduce anger or tension. Hence, “cool
down” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: This river is ____ than the one near our village.
questions.explanation:
(b) deeper
Comparative degree is used with ‘than’ to
make a comparison between two things.
‘Deeper’ is the correct comparative
degree of ‘deep’. Hence, ‘deeper’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: Hardly had the bell rung _____ the students rushed out of the classroom.
questions.explanation:
(a) when
“Hardly…when” is a fixed conjunction pair.
Hence, ‘when’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: She was ____ busy to attend the farewell party.
questions.explanation:
(c) too
‘Too’ is used to indicate an excessive
amount of something. ‘Too +
adjective(busy) + to + V1(attend)’ is the
correct grammatical structure. Hence,
‘too’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The singer performed ____ beautifully that the judges gave her a standing ovation.
questions.explanation:
(b) so
‘So’ is used to indicate a high degree of
something and is often followed by ‘that’
to show the result of the action. The
given sentence talks about how
beautifully the singer performed, leading
to the judges giving her a standing
ovation. Hence, ‘so’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense: In childhood, we _________ on the terrace during summer vacations.
questions.explanation:
(c) used to sleep
‘Used to’ is a semi-modal which indicates
a habitual action in the past. The given
sentence talks about a regular activity
done during childhood, sleeping on the
terrace during summer vacations. Hence,
‘used to sleep’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: This is the ______ chapter of the entire book.
questions.explanation:
(c) most interesting
‘Superlative degree’ denotes the form of
an adjective or adverb that expresses the
highest or a very high degree of quality of
a thing, person etc. ‘Most interesting’ is
the correct superlative form of
‘interesting’. Hence, ‘most interesting’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The phrase "The wind whispered through the trees" is an example of ______.
questions.explanation:
(c) personification
The phrase gives a human action
(whispered) to a non-human thing (wind).
This figure of speech is called
personification, as it attributes human
qualities to objects that are not human. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: He apologized ______ being late to the meeting.
questions.explanation:
(a) for
‘For’ is the fixed preposition used with
the verb ‘apologize’ when referring to the
reason. Hence, ‘for’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The boy ______ you met yesterday is my cousin.
questions.explanation:
(b) whom
‘Whom’ is used as the object of a verb or
preposition. In the sentence, the boy is
the object of the verb ‘met.’ Hence,
‘whom’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with suitable preposition: The cat is hiding ______ the table.
questions.explanation:
(b) under
‘Under’ is used to show that something is
below or beneath something else. In the
given sentence, the cat is beneath the
table. Hence, ‘under’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate adverb. He completed the assignment ______ and submitted it before the deadline.
questions.explanation:
(b) carefully
‘Carefully’ means doing something with
attention and caution. The sentence
suggests that the assignment was
completed with attention. Hence,
‘carefully’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: She solved the puzzle as __________ as an expert.
questions.explanation:
(c) quickly
The sentence requires an adverb to
modify the verb ‘solved’. “As + positive
degree + as” is the correct grammatical
structure. ‘Quickly’ is the positive degree
adverb. Hence, ‘quickly’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: If they ______ the truth, they would not have reacted that way.
questions.explanation:
(c) had known
The given sentence is an example of the
third conditional sentence and ‘If + past
perfect, … would have + V 3 ’ is the correct
grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘had
known’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: Rohan prefers science ______ commerce.
questions.explanation:
(d) to
‘To’ is a fixed preposition used with the
verb ‘prefer’. Hence, 'to' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate adverb: She finished her homework ________ than usual.
questions.explanation:
(b) quicker
Comparative degree is used with ‘than’
for comparison. The sentence compares
her speed of finishing homework. Hence,
“quicker” is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: This movie is _____ than the previous one we watched.
questions.explanation:
(b) more exciting
Comparative degree is used with ‘than’
for comparison between two entities.
Similarly, the given sentence compares
two movies. ‘More exciting’ is the correct
comparative degree. Hence, ‘more
exciting’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: The work must be __________ before the deadline.
questions.explanation:
(b) completed
‘Completed’ is the past participle form
used to indicate that the work is
expected to be finished. The given
sentence expresses completion of an
action before the deadline. Hence,
‘completed’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: Parents should look _______ their children properly.
questions.explanation:
(a) after
The phrase ‘look after’ means to take
care of someone. The sentence refers to
the responsibility of parents toward
children. Hence, ‘after’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: She spoke so _________ that everyone felt motivated.
questions.explanation:
(d) inspiringly
‘Inspiringly’ is the adverb showing the
manner of speaking. The given sentence
states that she spoke so inspiringly that
everyone felt motivated. Hence,
‘inspiringly’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with suitable preposition: She is _______ leave for two weeks due to medical reasons.
questions.explanation:
(b) on
‘On’ is the correct preposition used in the
phrase “on leave,” which means officially
permitted to be away from work or duty.
Hence, ‘on’ is the most appropriate
option. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
questions.explanation:
(c) will stay
The given sentence is an example of the
first conditional sentence and ‘If + simple
present, … will + V ’ is the correct
1
grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘will
stay ’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: Her ___ impressed everyone at the event.
questions.explanation:
(c) confidence
In the given sentence, the adjective ‘her’
requires a noun to follow it. Therefore,
the noun ‘confidence’ will be used.
Hence, ‘confidence’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: There isn’t _________ time left to finish the assignment.
questions.explanation:
(b) much
‘Much’ is used with uncountable nouns
like time to show quantity. The sentence
states that there isn’t enough time left.
Hence, ‘much’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense: He got a promotion after he ________ his project successfully.
questions.explanation:
(c) had completed
If two actions took place in the past, the
first action should be in the Past Perfect
tense (had + V 3), and the second action
should be in the Simple Past tense (V 2).
Hence, ‘had completed’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate collocation: She will try to ___________ progress in her English speaking skills.
questions.explanation:
(b) make
‘Make’ is the correct verb to use with the
word ‘progress’. Hence, ‘make’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: No sooner had he reached the station __________ the train departed.
questions.explanation:
(c) than
‘No sooner… than’ is a fixed conjunction
pair. Hence, ‘than’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb: The water in the river is __________ cold to swim in during winter.
questions.explanation:
(b) too
‘Too’ shows excess beyond a desirable
limit. The given sentence indicates
swimming is not possible because it is
excessively cold. Hence, ‘too’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the correct collocation in the following sentence. She wants to __________ her own fashion brand in the future.
questions.explanation:
(c) have
‘Have’ is used to express possession or
ownership. The given sentence talks
about owning a fashion brand in the
future. Hence, ‘have’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense: By the end of this year, they ____ the project successfully.
questions.explanation:
(c) will have completed
The sentence indicates an action that
will be finished by a specific future time.
Therefore, Future Perfect (will have + V 3 )
is required. Hence, ‘will have completed’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate collocation: He will __________ a speech at the annual function today.
questions.explanation:
(b) give
‘Give’ means to deliver or present
something to others. The given sentence
states that he will deliver a speech at the
annual function. Hence, ‘give’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the appropriate adverb: Do you remember the day _______ we first talked?
questions.explanation:
(b) when
‘When’ is a relative adverb used for time.
The sentence refers to a specific day
(time). Hence, ‘when’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate adverb: The baby slept _____throughout the night.
questions.explanation:
(b) quietly
The given sentence needs an adverb to
modify the verb ‘slept’. ‘Quietly’ is an
adverb of manner. Hence, ‘quietly’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate phrasal verb: The manager asked him to ______ the keys before leaving.
questions.explanation:
(b) hand over
The phrasal verb ‘hand over’ means to
give something to someone in authority
or control. The given sentence states
that the manager asked him to hand over
the keys. Hence, ‘hand over’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the correct article. Priya bought _____ umbrella and it turned out to be ____ useful item during the trip.
questions.explanation:
(a) an, a
We use ‘an’ before a vowel sounds like
‘umbrella’. The second blank needs an
indefinite article referring to the item
generally. Hence, ‘an, a’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collocation from the options below. He wants to ________ a complaint against the company.
questions.explanation:
(a) make
‘Make a complaint’ is the correct
collocation used when expressing
dissatisfaction formally. Hence, ‘make’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Identify the correct type of adjective in the following sentence. She has a beautiful voice. Here, beautiful is a ______ adjective.
questions.explanation:
(b) qualitative
‘Beautiful’ is a qualitative adjective, also
known as an adjective of quality. In the
given sentence, ‘beautiful’ describes the
quality of the noun ‘voice’. Hence,
‘qualitative’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: Mount Everest is the ____ mountain in the world.
questions.explanation:
(c) highest
We generally use the definite article ‘the’
before a superlative degree. Superlative
degree denotes the highest degree of a
quality among all people or things.
‘Highest’ is the correct superlative degree
of ‘high’. Hence, ‘highest’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with most appropriate option: The new model is not only faster but also ____ affordable than the previous one.
questions.explanation:
(c) more
As there is a comparative degree after
‘not only’, we have to use a comparative
degree after ‘but also’. ‘More affordable’
is the correct comparative degree.
Hence, ‘more’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks with the correct article. He wants to become ______ engineer and work in ______ United States.
questions.explanation:
(b) an, the
The given sentence talks about
engineers in general. Therefore, the
article ‘an’ will be used before ‘engineer’
as it starts with a vowel sound. We use
the definite article ‘the’ before the names
of countries when they represent a union
or federation like ‘the United States’.
Hence, ‘an, the’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct phrasal verb. The lights ___ suddenly during the storm.
questions.explanation:
(a) turned off
The phrasal verb ‘turned off’ means to
stop the supply of electricity or power.
The given sentence indicates that the
lights went off during the storm. Hence,
‘turned off’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition. They travelled ____ a train to Delhi.
questions.explanation:
(a) by
We generally use ‘by’ with public
transport and general modes of travel
such as “by train”, “by bus”, “by air”.
Hence, ‘by’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with suitable preposition: They walked slowly _______ the riverbank.
questions.explanation:
(a) along
‘Along’ is used to indicate movement
following the length or direction of
something. The sentence states that
they walked following the side of the
riverbank. Hence, ‘along’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The new policy proved far ____ than what the employees had expected.
questions.explanation:
(c) fairer
The given sentence indicates a
comparison between the new policy and
the expectations of the employees.
Therefore, comparative form ‘fairer’ is
required. Hence, ‘fairer’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Identify the correct type of pronoun in the following sentence. You should not hurt yourself while playing. Here, yourself is a _________ pronoun.
questions.explanation:
(b) reflexive
A reflexive pronoun is a pronoun that
refers back to the subject of a sentence.
For example:- myself, himself, herself,
yourself, themselves, itself, oneself,
ourselves, etc. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct phrasal verb: He promised to __________ the matter and provide a solution soon.
questions.explanation:
(b) look into
The phrasal verb “look into” means to
investigate or examine a matter. In the
given sentence, he promised to
investigate the issue and provide a
solution. Hence, ‘look into’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: When one linguistic expression refers back to another expression previously mentioned in the text, it is known as _______ reference.
questions.explanation:
(b) anaphoric
Anaphoric reference occurs when a word
refers back to something mentioned
earlier in the text. Hence, “anaphoric” is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The climber stood at the _____ of the cliff, looking down at the valley.
questions.explanation:
(b) brink
‘Brink’ means the extreme edge of land
before a steep drop. The given sentence
refers to the edge of a cliff. Hence, ‘brink’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the most suitable option to fill the blank part of the sentence. No sooner had the film been released than it was declared ________ successful movie of the year.
questions.explanation:
(c) the most
Superlative degree with ‘the’ is used to
show the highest quality among all. The
sentence refers to the most successful
movie of the year. Hence, ‘the most’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with an appropriate adverb. Riya felt __________ upset when her plans were cancelled.
questions.explanation:
(c) rather
‘Rather’ is used before adjectives to
express a fairly strong degree of
emotion. In this sentence, it emphasizes
that Riya was quite upset when her plans
were cancelled. Hence, ‘rather’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct option: We walked down the narrow __________ to reach the playground.
questions.explanation:
(c) lane
‘Lane’ is a narrow road or path. The
sentence refers to walking down a
narrow path. Hence, ‘lane’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Choose the option which best completes the sentence. When Rahul secured a job abroad, his parents were _____ with pride.
questions.explanation:
(a) on cloud nine
‘On cloud nine’ is an idiom that means
extremely happy and delighted. The
given sentence states that Rahul’s
achievement made his parents very
proud. Hence, ‘on cloud nine’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with an appropriate article. They visited _____ Himalayas during their winter vacation.
questions.explanation:
(c) the
We use the definite article ‘the’ for
mountain ranges, seas, and oceans.
Similarly, in the given sentence
‘Himalayas’ is a mountain range. Hence,
‘the’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The children built a small house out of wooden ______.
questions.explanation:
(b) blocks
'Blocks' are solid pieces of wood or other
material used for building models or
structures. The given sentence states
that the children built a small house out
of wooden blocks. Hence, 'blocks' is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Complete the collocation by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank. We should _______ attention in class if we want to learn effectively.
questions.explanation:
(a) pay
“Pay attention” is the correct collocation,
which means to listen or focus carefully.
The given sentence suggests that
students need to focus in class to learn
effectively. Hence, ‘pay’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The passengers gathered on the ship’s ___________ to enjoy the view of the sunset.
questions.explanation:
(b) deck
‘Deck’ means the floor or platform on a
ship where people can stand or walk. The
given sentence states that the
passengers gathered on the ship’s deck
to enjoy the view of the sunset. Hence,
‘deck’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct part of speech. The scientist made a remarkable ______ in the field of medicine.
questions.explanation:
(c) discovery
‘Discovery’ is a noun meaning a new
finding or invention. The given sentence
discusses an achievement in medicine.
Hence, ‘discovery’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The stars could be seen clearly in the sky at _____ .
questions.explanation:
(b) night
‘Night’ refers to the time after sunset and
before sunrise. The given sentence talks
about seeing stars, which happens at
night. Hence, ‘night’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with an appropriate phrasal verb. The teacher asked the students to take ______ the new rules carefully.
questions.explanation:
(b) down
The phrasal verb ‘take down’ means to
write something or note it. The given
sentence refers to noting new rules.
Hence, ‘take down’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with an appropriate degree of comparison. Out of all the subjects, Mathematics is the _______ difficult for me.
questions.explanation:
(b) most
‘Most’ is the superlative degree used
when comparing more than two things.
The given sentence refers to the highest
level of difficulty among all subjects.
Hence, ‘most’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The farmer walked across the muddy ______ after the rain.
questions.explanation:
(b) field
‘Field’ means an open land area used for
farming. The given sentence refers to a
farmer walking on land after rain. Hence,
‘field’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with appropriate prepositions. He is afraid ________ the dark and always keeps a light on.
questions.explanation:
(b) of
‘Of’ is the fixed preposition used after
‘afraid’ to express fear of something.
Hence, ‘of’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The walls are too thin; I can _______ every word they say.
questions.explanation:
(a) hear
‘Hear’ means to perceive sound with the
ears. The given sentence refers to
listening to words through thin walls.
Hence, ‘hear’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Complete the collocation by choosing a suitable word to fill in the blank. The doctor advised him to _______ a deep breath before speaking.
questions.explanation:
(a) take
‘Take a deep breath’ is the correct
collocation used when advising someone
to inhale deeply. The given sentence
suggests that the doctor advised him to
inhale deeply before speaking. Hence,
‘take’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: Only when he apologized __________ she forgive him.
questions.explanation:
(b) did
‘Did + V 1(forgive)’ is the correct
grammatical structure used in an
inverted sentence in the simple past
tense. Hence, ‘did’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The agreement was signed ______ mutual trust and understanding.
questions.explanation:
(b) under
‘Under’ is used to indicate that
something happens according to or
controlled by a particular condition. The
given sentence states that the
agreement was signed under the
condition of trust. Hence, ‘under’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: Either the principal or the teachers ______ responsible for organizing the event.
questions.explanation:
(b) are
“Neither….nor/ Either….or / Not only…but
also” is a conjunction pair that is used
only for two subjects, and the verb is
supplied according to the subject closest
to the verb. This is called the rule of
proximity. In the given sentence,
“teachers” is closest to the verb and
plural. So, it will take a plural verb. Hence,
‘are’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: Among all the research papers submitted this year, his study was regarded as the ____ contribution to environmental policy.
questions.explanation:
(b) most impactful
When we talk about the highest degree
of quality among all, the superlative
degree is used. The given sentence
refers to the most impactful contribution
among all papers. Hence, ‘most
impactful’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: Among all the proposals submitted, this was by far the ____ solution to the issue.
questions.explanation:
(c) best
We generally use the definite article ‘the’
before the superlative degree.
Superlative degree is used to express the
highest degree of quality of a person or
thing among all. The given sentence
refers to one proposal that stands out
among all the others. Hence, ‘best’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct option: This laptop is _________ than the previous model in terms of battery life.
questions.explanation:
(b) better
Comparative degree is used with ‘than’ to
compare two things. ‘Better’ is the
comparative degree of ‘good’. Hence,
‘better’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: This method is __________ than relying on manual calculations.
questions.explanation:
(c) more accurate
Comparative degree is used with ‘than’ to
compare two methods, things, or
persons. Similarly, the given sentence
compares two approaches. Hence, ‘more
accurate’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: It took several minutes for the shocking news to really ______.
questions.explanation:
(b) set in
‘Set in’ means something unpleasant
beginning and expected to continue. The
given sentence refers to the moment
when the shocking news began to be
realized. Hence, ‘set in’ is the most
